newsitem.title: SPAIN: European priests held in Zaire are well -- Spain.
newsitem.headline: European priests held in Zaire are well -- Spain.

text.p: The two European priests being held by Tutsi rebels at their mission in the eastern Zairean city of Bukavu were in good health, a Spanish Foreign Office official said on Thursday.
"They are still there, they are well," the spokeswoman told Reuters. "They are being held or kept under observation. There has been no personal injury."
All the priests at the Carmelite mission managed to flee the Tutsi attack on Wednesday except for Spanish priest Jesus Gutierrez Portero and a Belgian priest who was not identified.
Spanish ambassador to Zaire Jose Antonio Bordallo continued to negotiate their release.

An official at the aid organisation Medicos del Mundo (Doctors of the World) told the Spanish news agency Efe on Thursday that three Spanish aid workers were also trapped in fighting in eastern Zaire.
They were all in good health and in regular contact with Spanish diplomats in the area.
A male doctor with the non-governmental organisation was in Goma and had contacted colleagues in Madrid via satellite phone on Thursday to tell them he would try to leave Zaire by land or plane.
A male volunteer for Medicos del Mundo and female worker for Pharmaceuticals Without Borders were in Katale, 60 km (37 miles) north of Goma.
"They are being protected by the Zairean army," the official told Efe, adding that they were waiting for a plane or helicopter to take them out of the country.
Battles between Zairean troops and Tutsi rebels raged near Goma on Thursday and aid agencies responsible for feeding more than a million Hutu refugees prepared to evacuate.
But the Spanish official said Medicos del Mundo and its French counterpart were preparing a team of doctors and nurses to send to the zone as soon as humanitarian aid was let through.
